content:
The "local folder size" setting controls how many messages are downloaded. The default value is 25 and can be increased. You can find this in settings > account name > fetching mail.

The app will display "load up to 25 more" at the bottom of a mailbox while additional messages are available on the server. I'd recommend only downloading x number of recent messages, rather than your full mailbox

Developers recommend not increasing the value beyond 500. The app is known to have performance and stability issues when increased beyond this value. See their comments linked below.

https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-android/issues/10373

You can also set the age of messages to sync, for example, messages from the last 2 months. This can be helpful for people with very large mailbox's.

Navigate to settings > account name > fetching mail > sync messages from:

content:
Sounds like you overloaded the "fetch more" " queue Try, in order:

Give it 10-15 min on strong wifi — it may just be grinding through the backlog silently. Clear app cache: Android Settings → Apps → Thunderbird → Storage → Clear Cache (keeps your account, dumps the stuck sync). Force stop → reopen the app. Lower the sync limit: folder settings → "messages to keep synced" → smaller number (e.g. 25). Remove and re-add the account — since it's IMAP and your real email is untouched, this is zero-risk and guarantees a clean fetch.

Since you rarely use the phone for email anyway, I'd skip straight to clearing the cache, and if that doesn't work in a minute or two, just remove/re-add the account.

content:
It seems the thing is that the phone has to grab the email before the computer gets it and deletes it from the server.

Yes, that makes sense. The account is likely configured on your computer to use the legacy pop protocol. Possibly also on your phone if you imported the same config.

Pop is designed for use on a single device. It typically downloads and stores the email locally on the device. Once downloaded, the email is typically deleted on the server. You can read more about pop v imap at the link below.

https://thetechylife.com/should-i-choose-imap-or-pop3/
